reason: A measured dimension (length of the leaf lamina, PO_0020039), not a structure; the examples are ratios to the leaf (pattern 10) or vein-extent statements. Same as the earlier 'leaf length' decision.
Narrower: a floret is a small flower of a dense inflorescence (earlier decision floret -> flower PO_0009046), and 'male flower' is a PO synonym of staminate flower.
A 'per X' counting phrase (sori per ultimate leaf segment), not a structure. The earlier review rejected 'per segment' and 'ultimate segment' in the same way.
Narrower: a hair-like pappus element; PO lists 'pappus bristle' as a synonym.
Narrower: the stalk of a Marsileaceae sporocarp. PO has no sporocarp class, so the whole cannot be stated yet; sporocarp itself is worth proposing to PO.

French 'pair', a counting unit ('3 paires de folioles' = 6 leaflets in 3 pairs); count of parts (pattern 03; cf. 'jugate' in flora_counted_parts). The earlier review rejected 'pair' as not a structure.

label: loment segment
parent: is_a PO_0025498 (cardinal part of multi-tissue plant structure); part_of PO_0030101 (loment fruit)
definition: A cardinal part of multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025498) that is one of the transverse, usually one-seeded, indehiscent segments into which a loment fruit (PO:0030101) breaks at maturity. NOTE: PO defines loment fruit by these segments but has no class for them; not a mericarp (PO:0020075), which is a carpellate unit. Propose to PO upstream.
reason: A real structure that legume floras (Desmodium, Aeschynomene, Hedysarum and others) describe with shape, size and number; PO uses it in a definition but has no class for it.
Narrower: the fleshy or dry scale leaves of a bulb. Fibrous outer coats are better grounded to tunic (FLOPO_0986041).

target: spine leaf (PO_0025173) part_of areole bud (PO_0025353), position subcentral in the areole
reason: Narrower: a cactus spine is a spine leaf of the areole bud. 'Subcentral' is a position in the series radial/subcentral/central, which the position pattern can carry.

target: perigynium (PO_0009044), tooth of its apex (beak) region
reason: A Carex perigynium beak ends in teeth; this is an apical region of an existing class, and PO has no beak class.
A ratio to another part (pattern 10), not a structure. The other part, the trophophore, is the sterile blade of an Ophioglossaceae leaf.
Unclear without context: could be floral-disc lobes, disk-floret corolla lobes, or pappus/corona segments. 'Ligulate' and 'spatulate' do not settle which.

Narrower: in Iris the falls are the three outer, usually down-curved tepals. The outer whorl is a position. Restrict to Iridaceae context, because 'fall' is also a verb.

A pore in the wall of a Sphagnum hyaline cell. PO has no hyaline cell (hyalocyst) and a wall pore is not a PO-kind structure. Most statements are counts per cell (see 'pores per cell'). Revisit only together with a hyaline cell class.
Narrower: a tooth or segment of the inner peristome (endostome) of a moss capsule.
Narrower: in mosses (Sphagnum etc.) branch leaves are set against stem leaves. If the flora is vascular, use leaf (PO_0025034) on branch instead.
Unclear: 'flotteurs' may be the spongy floating roots of Ludwigia (pneumatophore PO_0025357) or the inflated petioles of Trapa or Eichhornia. 'Hairy' and 'whorled' do not settle which.

The female gametangium of Characeae or Vaucheria (algae), outside PO's scope. Mapping it to a land-plant gametangium class would be doubtful.
Unclear: the persistent remains of perianth, style or stamens on the fruit. Which organ it is cannot be told without context; persistence should go on that organ.
A count of seeds (PO_0009010) per fruit valve (PO_0000033), not a structure; same as the earlier 'seeds per locule'.
Narrower: separate glands on top of an inferior ovary, i.e. disc glands in epigynous position.

The margin of an existing class, expressed with the region pattern; winged, serrulate and flat apply to the margin.

Narrower: in Pottiaceae and similar mosses the outer peristome is split into 32 filiform teeth or tooth divisions; these are the peristome teeth themselves.
